newsitem.title: USA: Suspect in California cremation case found dead.
newsitem.headline: Suspect in California cremation case found dead.

text.p: Authorities on Wednesday identified the body of a missing pilot who allegedly put thousands of boxes of cremated human remains in storage after he was hired to spread them over mountains and at sea.
Sheriff's deputies said the pilot, Allan Vieira, appeared to have committed suicide.
Investigators have been searching for weeks for the pilot, who operates the Vieira Flying Service. Authorities believe he was hired by funeral homes in California to spread the ashes.

Instead, sheriff's deputies said he placed more than 5,000 boxes of the cremated remains in public storage lockers in Discovery Bay, about 45 miles (72 kms) east of San Francisco, and at a nearby hangar where he kept a plane.
The macabre discovery of the remains traumatized families of the deceased, shocked California residents and baffled investigators.
Vieira's badly decomposed body and a handgun were found just south of San Andreas, about 100 miles (160 kms) east of San Francisco, near an abandoned car.
Boxes of cremated human remains were found in the car along with a note saying "Sorry for the pain I've caused!" The note was dated June 5.
The Calaveras County Coroner's office said it used dental records to identify the body.
The cause of death was a single gunshot wound to the head, Detective Ethel Mitchell said.
"It is consistent with a self-inflicted gunshot wound," she added.
Most of the boxes of ashes had name tags and dates, identifying the deceased and when they were cremated. Investigators have been able to return many of the ashes to the families.
"There are a lot of anxious families out there," Sgt. Jerry Knutson said. "There are a lot of upset people."
